recall.q: Why does GDP count only final goods and services, and what does value added do?
recall.a: Summing every sale counts each input again at every later stage. Count final sales, or each stage's sales minus its input purchases (value added). Used goods and transfers are left out.

recall.q: Nominal GDP is 1,320 and the GDP deflator is 110. What is real GDP?
recall.a: 1,320 ÷ 1.10 = 1,200. Divide by deflator ÷ 100; taking 10% off (1,188) is wrong.

recall.q: Private saving is 600, investment 450 and the government deficit (G − T) 200. What is the trade balance, and what does it mean?
recall.a: X − M = S − I − (G − T) = 600 − 450 − 200 = −50: a trade deficit, funded by borrowing 50 from abroad. It is an identity and says nothing about cause.

recall.q: An oil shock shifts SRAS left. What happens to output and the price level in the short run, and why can't a demand shift do the same?
recall.a: Output falls and prices rise (stagflation). A demand shift moves output and prices the same way; only a supply shift moves them in opposite directions.

recall.q: TFP grows 0.5%, labour 0.8% and capital 2.5%, with income shares of 0.7 for labour and 0.3 for capital. What is potential GDP growth, and which part can last?
recall.a: 0.5 + 0.7 × 0.8 + 0.3 × 2.5 = 0.5 + 0.56 + 0.75 = 1.81%. Only TFP growth lasts: more capital per worker runs into diminishing returns.

recall.q: How do you get from GDP to national income, and from personal income to personal disposable income?
recall.a: National income = GDP − capital consumption allowance (depreciation) − statistical discrepancy. Personal disposable income = personal income − personal taxes.

recall.q: Your two calculator checks: what should 3 + 2 × 4 = show, and what FV should 2ND CLR TVM, 5 N, 8 I/Y, 1000 +|− PV, 0 PMT, CPT FV give? What do 20.0000 and 1,033.7808 mean?
recall.a: 11.0000 and 1,469.3281. 20.0000 means chain mode is still on (set AOS); 1,033.7808 means P/Y is 12 (set P/Y = 1).
